A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCLD work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices through A.6.10 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCLD sampling experiments, including ELBO and Sinkhorn results in Tables 2–3, component ablations and further appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and appendix investigations, including MCMC ablations, prior-initialization studies and KL-versus-LV comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 retain the same controlled diffusion, importance weighting, resampling, MCMC refinements and replay-buffer training. The adaptive-annealing alternative discussed in v2 is explicitly future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 principal benchmarks and supplementary scenarios, including the two-dimensional GMM illustration and Funnel dimensionality sweep. No evaluated dataset, task or domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: SMC variants, CRAFT, DDS, PIS, CMCD-KL/LV and the appendix PDDS variants. Newly cited methods such as NETS are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections A.5–A.6 retain the same metrics, 2000 evaluation particles, diffusion-step settings, architectures, training budgets and hyperparameter-selection procedures. The new adaptive-annealing discussion does not report an implemented protocol change.

E4.justification: The component and MCMC ablations, learned-annealing visualization, MFVI mode-collapse study and KL/LV dimensional-scaling analysis are retained unchanged. Relocated appendix figures do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: The four-seed main evaluation, three-seed convergence plots and ten-seed SMC-ESS evaluation remain documented in both versions. Existing uncertainty displays and ± reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, SCLD's Robot4 Sinkhorn distance remains 0.40±0.01 in Table 3, and SCLD-MFVI's LGCP ELBO remains 500.56±0.12 in Table 11.

T1.justification: Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.3 and the appendix proofs remain substantively identical. Equation (31) merely makes the identity-matrix factor explicit in the already isotropic Gaussian covariances. Changed cross-reference names do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous-time unification, off-policy training, loss scaling, sampling performance and reduced training budgets.

C2.justification: Section A.3.2 newly explains how fixing β(t)=t and adapting the time discretization through a constant-ESS scheme could replace learned annealing, explicitly leaving investigation to future work. This adds a specific explanation of design flexibility; existing result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit SCLD code-repository link in Section 3, footnote 4, which v1 lacks. Existing pseudocode, implementation settings, hardware information and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Section A.1 and the references add six works, including NETS and Vaikuntanathan and Jarzynski's historical contribution. v2 acknowledges NETS as concurrent work combining learned SDE sampling with resampling, refining the earlier positioning centered on PDDS.

P1.justification: Affiliations, publication headers and cross-reference terminology change, with limited new explanatory prose and the same overall section structure. Several references now incorrectly say 'Theorem' although the referenced items remain labeled Lemma, Proposition or Remark.

P2.justification: All 15 tables and 11 figures retain their content and display structures, but appendix floats move relative to the prose. Figure 10 moves below its subsection heading, while Figure 11 moves to a separate final page.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer in Section 3 and acknowledgment of concurrent and historical work in A.1 modestly improve reproducibility documentation and research positioning. These gains outweigh the limited cross-reference naming errors. The method, proofs and empirical support remain unchanged.
